findings.title: Other sub-group methods still NPE when the group is deleted concurrently
findings.body: Only `getSubGroupsCount()` gets the null guard. The three `getSubGroupsStream(...)` overloads (lines 256, 262, 268) still call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` with no null check. `modelSupplier` returns null when the group was deleted by another transaction after the cached entry was read, which is exactly the race this PR targets. A concurrent delete plus a sub-group listing through the cache adapter will therefore still throw the same NPE. Apply the same null handling (or a consistent not-found behaviour) to all delegating methods so the fix is not partial.

findings.title: getSubGroupsCount() now silently returns null for a deleted group
findings.body: When the backing group no longer exists, `getSubGroupsCount()` returns `null` instead of failing. The `GroupModel` contract does not document a null result. Any caller that unboxes the `Long` (for example `getSubGroupsCount() > 0`) will now NPE somewhere else, and callers that only copy it into a representation will emit a null count that looks like valid data. The null return and the reasoning behind it should be documented, or the caller (`GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount`) should handle it explicitly. The null return also differs from the other adapter methods, which throw `IllegalStateException("Not found in database")` for a missing group.

findings.title: Concurrency test leaves reader thread unjoined, so results are racy and the thread can outlive the test
findings.body: The reader thread is started with `new Thread(...).start()` and never joined. After `deletedAll.set(true)` the test immediately asserts `caughtExceptions` is empty. The thread may be mid-request at that point, so an exception from the last iteration can be added after the assertion has already passed, which makes the test unreliable. The thread can also keep calling the admin client after the test ends and the realm is cleaned up. Keep a reference to the thread and `join()` it (with a timeout) before asserting. The loop also has no pacing, so it hammers the server with `Integer.MAX_VALUE` page sizes. Nothing guarantees the read overlaps the deletes, so the test may pass without ever exercising the race.
